Added in [API level 8](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

# DevicePolicyManager

```
open class DevicePolicyManager
```

| [kotlin.Any](https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-any/index.html) ||
| --- | --- |
| ↳ | [android.app.admin.DevicePolicyManager](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) |

Manages device policy and restrictions applied to the user of the device or apps running on the device.

This class contains three types of methods:

1. Those aimed at [managing apps](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md)
2. Those aimed at the [Device Policy Management Role Holder](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md)
3. Those aimed at [apps which wish to respect device policy](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md)

The intended caller for each API is indicated in its Javadoc.

**Managing Apps**

Apps can be made capable of setting device policy ("Managing Apps") either by being set as a [Device Administrator](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md), being set as a [Device Policy Controller](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md), or by holding the appropriate [Permissions](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md).

A **Device Administrator** is an app which is able to enforce device policies that it has declared in its device admin XML file. An app can prompt the user to give it device administrator privileges using the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_ADD_DEVICE_ADMIN:kotlin.String` action.

For more information about Device Administration, read the [Device Administration](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/admin/device-admin.html) developer guide.

Device Administrator apps can also be recognised as **Device Policy Controllers**. Device Policy Controllers can be one of two types:

- A *Device Owner* , which only ever exists on the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#isSystemUser()` or Main User, is the most powerful type of Device Policy Controller and can affect policy across the device.
- A *Profile Owner* , which can exist on any user, can affect policy on the user it is on, and when it is running on `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#isProfile()` has [limited](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) ability to affect policy on its parent.

Additional capabilities can be provided to Device Policy Controllers in the following circumstances:

- A Profile Owner on an [organization owned](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) device has access to additional abilities, both [affecting policy on the profile's](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) parent and also the profile itself.
- A Profile Owner running on the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#isSystemUser()` has access to additional capabilities which affect the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#isSystemUser()` and also the whole device.
- A Profile Owner running on an [affiliated](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) user has capabilities similar to that of a [Device Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md)

For more information, see [Building a Device Policy Controller](https://developer.android.com/work/dpc/build-dpc).

[Permissions](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) are generally only given to apps fulfilling particular key roles on the device (such as managing `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/devicelock/DeviceLockManager.html#`).

**Device Policy Management Role Holder**

One app on the device fulfills the Device Policy Management Role and is trusted with managing the overall state of Device Policy. This has access to much more powerful methods than [managing apps](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md).

**Querying Device Policy**

In most cases, regular apps do not need to concern themselves with device policy, and restrictions will be enforced automatically. There are some cases where an app may wish to query device policy to provide a better user experience. Only a small number of policies allow apps to query them directly. These APIs will typically have no special required permissions.

**Managed Provisioning**

Managed Provisioning is the process of recognising an app as a [Device Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) or [Profile Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md). It involves presenting education and consent screens to the user to ensure they are aware of the capabilities this grants the [Device Policy Controller](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md)

For more information on provisioning, see [Building a Device Policy Controller](https://developer.android.com/work/dpc/build-dpc).

A **Managed Profile** enables data separation. For example to use a device both for personal and corporate usage. The managed profile and its parent share a launcher.

**Affiliation**

Using the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setAffiliationIds(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.collections.MutableSet)` method, a [Device Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) can set a list of affiliation ids for the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#isSystemUser()`. Any [Profile Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) on the same device can also call `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setAffiliationIds(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.collections.MutableSet)` to set affiliation ids for the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#` it is on. When there is the same ID present in both lists, the user is said to be "affiliated" and we can refer to the [Profile Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) as a "profile owner on an affiliated user" or an "affiliated profile owner". Becoming affiliated grants the [Profile Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) capabilities similar to that of the [Device Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md). It also allows use of the #bindDeviceAdminServiceAsUser APIs for direct communication between the [Device Owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) and affiliated [Profile Owners](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md).

**Organization Owned**
An organization owned device is one which is not owned by the person making use of the device and is instead owned by an organization such as their employer or education provider. These devices are recognised as being organization owned either by the presence of a [device owner](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) or of a `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#isOrganizationOwnedDeviceWithManagedProfile()`.

Profile owners running on an [organization owned](../android/app/admin/organization-owned.md) device can exercise additional capabilities using the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getParentProfileInstance(android.content.ComponentName)` API which apply to the parent user. Each API will indicate if it is usable in this way.

**Android Automotive**

On `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/pm/PackageManager.html#FEATURE_AUTOMOTIVE:kotlin.String`, some methods can throw `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/UnsafeStateException` if an action is unsafe (for example, if the vehicle is moving). Callers running on `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/pm/PackageManager.html#FEATURE_AUTOMOTIVE:kotlin.String` should always check for this exception. 
Restricted for SDK Runtime environment in API level 34. 
Requires the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/pm/PackageManager.html#FEATURE_DEVICE_ADMIN:kotlin.String` feature which can be detected using `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/pm/PackageManager.html#hasSystemFeature(kotlin.String)`.

## Constants

### ACTION_ADD_DEVICE_ADMIN

Added in [API level 8](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_ADD_DEVICE_ADMIN: String
```

Activity action: ask the user to add a new device administrator to the system. The desired policy is the ComponentName of the policy in the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_DEVICE_ADMIN:kotlin.String` extra field. This will invoke a UI to bring the user through adding the device administrator to the system (or allowing them to reject it).

You can optionally include the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_ADD_EXPLANATION:kotlin.String` field to provide the user with additional explanation (in addition to your component's description) about what is being added.

If your administrator is already active, this will ordinarily return immediately (without user intervention). However, if your administrator has been updated and is requesting additional uses-policy flags, the user will be presented with the new list. New policies will not be available to the updated administrator until the user has accepted the new list.

 Value: "android.app.action.ADD_DEVICE_ADMIN"

### ACTION_ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE

Added in [API level 29](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE: String
```

Activity action: Starts the administrator to show policy compliance for the provisioning. This action is used any time that the administrator has an opportunity to show policy compliance before the end of setup wizard. This could happen as part of the admin-integrated provisioning flow (in which case this gets sent after `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_GET_PROVISIONING_MODE:kotlin.String`), or it could happen during provisioning finalization if the administrator supports finalization during setup wizard.

Intents with this action may also be supplied with the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String` extra.

 Value: "android.app.action.ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE"

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_GET_PROVISIONING_MODE:kotlin.String`

### ACTION_APPLICATION_DELEGATION_SCOPES_CHANGED

Added in [API level 26](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_APPLICATION_DELEGATION_SCOPES_CHANGED: String
```

Broadcast Action: Sent after application delegation scopes are changed. The new delegation scopes will be sent in an `ArrayList<String>` extra identified by the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_DELEGATION_SCOPES:kotlin.String` key.

**Note:** This is a protected intent that can only be sent by the system.

 Value: "android.app.action.APPLICATION_DELEGATION_SCOPES_CHANGED"

### ACTION_CHECK_POLICY_COMPLIANCE

Added in [API level 30](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_CHECK_POLICY_COMPLIANCE: String
```

Activity action: launch the DPC to check policy compliance. This intent is launched when the user taps on the notification about personal apps suspension. When handling this intent the DPC must check if personal apps should still be suspended and either unsuspend them or instruct the user on how to resolve the noncompliance causing the suspension.

 Value: "android.app.action.CHECK_POLICY_COMPLIANCE"

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setPersonalAppsSuspended(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)`

### ACTION_DEVICE_ADMIN_SERVICE

Added in [API level 26](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_DEVICE_ADMIN_SERVICE: String
```

Service action: Action for a service that device owner and profile owner can optionally own. If a device owner or a profile owner has such a service, the system tries to keep a bound connection to it, in order to keep their process always running. The service must be protected with the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#BIND_DEVICE_ADMIN:kotlin.String` permission.

 Value: "android.app.action.DEVICE_ADMIN_SERVICE"

### ACTION_DEVICE_FINANCING_STATE_CHANGED

Added in [API level 34](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_DEVICE_FINANCING_STATE_CHANGED: String
```

Broadcast Action: Broadcast sent to indicate that the device financing state has changed.

This occurs when, for example, a financing kiosk app has been added or removed.

To query the current device financing state see `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#isDeviceFinanced()`.

This will be delivered to the following apps if they include a receiver for this action in their manifest:

- Device owner admins.
- Organization-owned profile owner admins
- The supervision app
- The device management role holder

 Value: "android.app.admin.action.DEVICE_FINANCING_STATE_CHANGED"

static val ACTION_DEVICE_OWNER_CHANGED: String

### ACTION_DEVICE_POLICY_RESOURCE_UPDATED

Added in [API level 33](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_DEVICE_POLICY_RESOURCE_UPDATED: String
```

Broadcast action: notify system apps (e.g. settings, SysUI, etc) that the device management resources with IDs `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_RESOURCE_IDS:kotlin.String` has been updated, the updated resources can be retrieved using android.app.admin.DevicePolicyResourcesManager#getDrawable and android.app.admin.DevicePolicyResourcesManager#getString.

This broadcast is sent to registered receivers only.

`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_RESOURCE_TYPE:kotlin.String` will be included to identify the type of resource being updated.

 Value: "android.app.action.DEVICE_POLICY_RESOURCE_UPDATED"

### ACTION_GET_PROVISIONING_MODE

Added in [API level 29](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_GET_PROVISIONING_MODE: String
```

Activity action: Starts the administrator to get the mode for the provisioning. This intent may contain the following extras:

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_IMEI:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SERIAL_NUMBER:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ALLOWED_PROVISIONING_MODES:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SENSORS_PERMISSION_GRANT_OPT_OUT:kotlin.String`

<br />

The target activity should return one of the following values in `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_MODE:kotlin.String` as result:

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#PROVISIONING_MODE_FULLY_MANAGED_DEVICE:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#PROVISIONING_MODE_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.Int`

If performing fully-managed device provisioning and the admin app desires to show its own education screens, the target activity can additionally return `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SKIP_EDUCATION_SCREENS:kotlin.String` set to `true`.

The target activity may also return the account that needs to be migrated from primary user to managed profile in case of a profile owner provisioning in `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ACCOUNT_TO_MIGRATE:kotlin.String` as result.

The target activity may also include the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String` extra in the intent result. The values of this `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/PersistableBundle.html#` will be sent as an intent extra of the same name to the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE:kotlin.String` activity, along with the values of the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String` extra that are already supplied to this activity.

Other extras the target activity may include in the intent result:

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMERS:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SKIP_ENCRYPTION:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_KEEP_SCREEN_ON:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_KEEP_ACCOUNT_ON_MIGRATION:kotlin.String` for work profile provisioning
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LEAVE_ALL_SYSTEM_APPS_ENABLED:kotlin.String` for work profile provisioning
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SENSORS_PERMISSION_GRANT_OPT_OUT:kotlin.String` for fully-managed device provisioning
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LOCALE:kotlin.String` for fully-managed device provisioning
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LOCAL_TIME:kotlin.String` for fully-managed device provisioning
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_TIME_ZONE:kotlin.String` for fully-managed device provisioning

 Value: "android.app.action.GET_PROVISIONING_MODE"

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE:kotlin.String`

### ACTION_MANAGED_PROFILE_PROVISIONED

Added in [API level 23](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_MANAGED_PROFILE_PROVISIONED: String
```

Broadcast Action: This broadcast is sent to indicate that provisioning of a managed profile has completed successfully.

The broadcast is limited to the primary profile, to the app specified in the provisioning intent with action `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.String`.

This intent will contain the following extras

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#EXTRA_USER:kotlin.String`, corresponds to the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserHandle.html#` of the managed profile.
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ACCOUNT_TO_MIGRATE:kotlin.String`, corresponds to the account requested to be migrated at provisioning time, if any.

 Value: "android.app.action.MANAGED_PROFILE_PROVISIONED"

static val ACTION_PROFILE_OWNER_CHANGED: String
```

Broadcast action: sent when the profile owner is set, changed or cleared. This broadcast is sent only to the user managed by the new profile owner.

### ACTION_PROVISIONING_SUCCESSFUL

Added in [API level 26](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_PROVISIONING_SUCCESSFUL: String
```

Activity action: This activity action is sent to indicate that provisioning of a managed profile or managed device has completed successfully. It'll be sent at the same time as `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver#ACTION_PROFILE_PROVISIONING_COMPLETE:kotlin.String` broadcast but this will be delivered faster as it's an activity intent.

The intent is only sent to the new device or profile owner.

 Value: "android.app.action.PROVISIONING_SUCCESSFUL"

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.String`

### ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_DEVICE

Added in [API level 23](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels) 
Deprecated in [API level 31](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_DEVICE: String
```

**Deprecated:** *to support `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#S:kotlin.Int` and later, admin apps must implement activities with intent filters for the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_GET_PROVISIONING_MODE:kotlin.String` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_ADMIN_POLICY_COMPLIANCE:kotlin.String` intent actions; using `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_DEVICE:kotlin.String` to start provisioning will cause the provisioning to fail; to additionally support pre-`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#S:kotlin.Int`, admin apps must also continue to use this constant.*

Activity action: Starts the provisioning flow which sets up a managed device. Must be started with `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/Activity.html#startActivityForResult(android.content.Intent,%20kotlin.Int)`.

During device owner provisioning a device admin app is set as the owner of the device. A device owner has full control over the device. The device owner can not be modified by the user.

A typical use case would be a device that is owned by a company, but used by either an employee or client.

An intent with this action can be sent only on an unprovisioned device. It is possible to check if provisioning is allowed or not by querying the method `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#isProvisioningAllowed(kotlin.String)`.

The intent contains the following extras:

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_COMPONENT_NAME:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SKIP_ENCRYPTION:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LEAVE_ALL_SYSTEM_APPS_ENABLED:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LOGO_URI:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMERS:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SKIP_EDUCATION_SCREENS:kotlin.String`, optional

When device owner provisioning has completed, an intent of the type `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver#ACTION_PROFILE_PROVISIONING_COMPLETE:kotlin.String` is broadcast to the device owner.

From version `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#O:kotlin.Int`, when device owner provisioning has completed, along with the above broadcast, activity intent `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISIONING_SUCCESSFUL:kotlin.String` will also be sent to the device owner.

If provisioning fails, the device is factory reset.

A result code of `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/Activity.html#RESULT_OK:kotlin.Int` implies that the synchronous part of the provisioning flow was successful, although this doesn't guarantee the full flow will succeed. Conversely a result code of `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/Activity.html#RESULT_CANCELED:kotlin.Int` implies that the user backed-out of provisioning, or some precondition for provisioning wasn't met.

 Value: "android.app.action.PROVISION_MANAGED_DEVICE"

| `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String` | ||

| `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SKIP_USER_CONSENT:kotlin.String` | **Can only be used by an existing device owner trying to create a managed profile** ||

Must match the package name of the calling application.** | `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#LOLLIPOP:kotlin.Int`+ |
| `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_COMPONENT_NAME:kotlin.String` | **Required if `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_NAME:kotlin.String` is not specified. Package name must match the package name of the calling application.** | `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#M:kotlin.Int`+ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ALLOW_OFFLINE:kotlin.String` | On `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#TIRAMISU:kotlin.Int`+, when set to true this will **force** offline provisioning instead of allowing it ||

When [managed provisioning](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) has completed, broadcasts are sent to the application specified in the provisioning intent. The `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver#ACTION_PROFILE_PROVISIONING_COMPLETE:kotlin.String` broadcast is sent in the managed profile and the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_MANAGED_PROFILE_PROVISIONED:kotlin.String` broadcast is sent in the primary profile.

From version `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#O:kotlin.Int`, when managed provisioning has completed, along with the above broadcast, activity intent `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISIONING_SUCCESSFUL:kotlin.String` will also be sent to the profile owner.

If provisioning fails, the managed profile is removed so the device returns to its previous state.

If launched with `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/Activity.html#startActivityForResult(android.content.Intent,%20kotlin.Int)` a result code of `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/Activity.html#RESULT_OK:kotlin.Int` indicates that the synchronous part of the provisioning flow was successful, although this doesn't guarantee the full flow will succeed. Conversely a result code of `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/Activity.html#RESULT_CANCELED:kotlin.Int` indicates that the user backed-out of provisioning or some precondition for provisioning wasn't met.

If a [device policy management role holder](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md) updater is present on the device, an internet connection attempt must be made prior to launching this intent.

 Value: "android.app.action.PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE"

### ACTION_SET_NEW_PARENT_PROFILE_PASSWORD

Added in [API level 24](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_SET_NEW_PARENT_PROFILE_PASSWORD: String
```

Activity action: have the user enter a new password for the parent profile. If the intent is launched from within a managed profile, this will trigger entering a new password for the parent of the profile. The caller can optionally set `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_DEVICE_PASSWORD_REQUIREMENT_ONLY:kotlin.String` to only enforce device-wide password requirement. In all other cases the behaviour is identical to `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_SET_NEW_PASSWORD:kotlin.String`.

 Value: "android.app.action.SET_NEW_PARENT_PROFILE_PASSWORD"

### ACTION_SET_NEW_PASSWORD

Added in [API level 8](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ACTION_SET_NEW_PASSWORD: String
```

Activity action: have the user enter a new password.

For admin apps, this activity should be launched after using `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setPasswordQuality(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Int)`, or `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setPasswordMinimumLength(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Int)` to have the user enter a new password that meets the current requirements. You can use `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#isActivePasswordSufficient()` to determine whether you need to have the user select a new password in order to meet the current constraints. Upon being resumed from this activity, you can check the new password characteristics to see if they are sufficient.

Non-admin apps can use `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getPasswordComplexity()` to check the current screen lock complexity, and use this activity with extra `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY:kotlin.String` to suggest to users how complex the app wants the new screen lock to be. Note that both `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getPasswordComplexity()` and the extra `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY:kotlin.String` require the calling app to have the permission `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#REQUEST_PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY:kotlin.String`.

If the intent is launched from within a managed profile with a profile owner built against `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#M:kotlin.Int` or before, this will trigger entering a new password for the parent of the profile. For all other cases it will trigger entering a new password for the user or profile it is launched from.

 Value: "android.app.action.SET_NEW_PASSWORD"

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_SET_NEW_PARENT_PROFILE_PASSWORD:kotlin.String`

### ACTION_START_ENCRYPTION

Added in [API level 11](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```

```

Activity action: begin the process of encrypting data on the device. This activity should be launched after using `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` to request encryption be activated. After resuming from this activity, use `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName)` to check encryption status. However, on some devices this activity may never return, as it may trigger a reboot and in some cases a complete data wipe of the device.

Added in [API level 29](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```

```

Grants access to selection of KeyChain certificates on behalf of requesting apps. There can be at most one app that has this delegation. If another app already had delegated certificate selection access, it will lose the delegation when a new app is delegated.

The delegated app can also call #grantKeyPairToApp and #revokeKeyPairFromApp to directly grant KeyChain keys to other apps.

Can be granted by Device Owner or Profile Owner.

### ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE

Added in [API level 11](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE: Int
```

Result code for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()`: indicating that encryption is active.

`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()` can only return this value for apps targeting API level 23 or lower, or on devices that use Full Disk Encryption. Support for Full Disk Encryption was entirely removed in API level 33, having been replaced by File Based Encryption. The result code `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE_PER_USER:kotlin.Int` is used on devices that use File Based Encryption, except when the app targets API level 23 or lower.

`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` can still return this value for an unrelated reason, but `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` is deprecated since it doesn't do anything useful.

 Value: 3

### ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE_DEFAULT_KEY

Added in [API level 23](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE_DEFAULT_KEY: Int
```

Result code for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()`: indicating that encryption is active, but the encryption key is not cryptographically protected by the user's credentials.

This value can only be returned on devices that use Full Disk Encryption. Support for Full Disk Encryption was entirely removed in API level 33, having been replaced by File Based Encryption. With File Based Encryption, each user's credential-encrypted storage is always cryptographically protected by the user's credentials.

 Value: 4

### ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE_PER_USER

```

```

Result code for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()`: indicating that encryption is active and the encryption key is tied to the user or profile.

This value is only returned to apps targeting API level 24 and above. For apps targeting earlier API levels, `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE:kotlin.Int` is returned, even if the encryption key is specific to the user or profile.

 Value: 5

### ENCRYPTION_STATUS_INACTIVE

Added in [API level 11](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val ENCRYPTION_STATUS_INACTIVE: Int
```

Result code for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()`: indicating that encryption is supported, but is not currently active.

`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()` can only return this value on devices that use Full Disk Encryption. Support for Full Disk Encryption was entirely removed in API level 33, having been replaced by File Based Encryption. Devices that use File Based Encryption always automatically activate their encryption on first boot.

`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` can still return this value for an unrelated reason, but `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setStorageEncryption(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)` is deprecated since it doesn't do anything useful.

```

A boolean extra for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_SET_NEW_PARENT_PROFILE_PASSWORD:kotlin.String` requesting that only device password requirement is enforced during the parent profile password enrolment flow.

Normally when enrolling password for the parent profile, both the device-wide password requirement (requirement set via `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getParentProfileInstance(android.content.ComponentName)` instance) and the profile password requirement are enforced, if the profile currently does not have a separate work challenge. A ComponentName extra indicating the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver` of the application that will be set as the [Device Policy Controller](../android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager.md).

### EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_CHECKSUM

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_CHECKSUM: String
```

A String extra holding the URL-safe base64 encoded SHA-256 hash of the file at download location specified in `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_LOCATION:kotlin.String`.

Either this extra or `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_SIGNATURE_CHECKSUM:kotlin.String` must be present. The provided checksum must match the checksum of the file at the download location. If the checksum doesn't match an error will be shown to the user and the user will be asked to factory reset the device.

Use in an NFC record with `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#MIME_TYPE_PROVISIONING_NFC:kotlin.String` that starts device owner provisioning via an NFC bump. It can also be used for QR code provisioning.

**Note:** for devices running `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#LOLLIPOP:kotlin.Int` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#LOLLIPOP_MR1:kotlin.Int` only SHA-1 hash is supported. Starting from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#M:kotlin.Int`, this parameter accepts SHA-256 in addition to SHA-1. From `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`, only SHA-256 hash is supported.

 Value: "android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_CHECKSUM"

### EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMERS

Added in [API level 26](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMERS: String
```

A `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Bundle.html#`\[\] extra consisting of list of disclaimer headers and disclaimer contents.

Each `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Bundle.html#` must have both `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_HEADER:kotlin.String` as disclaimer header, and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_CONTENT:kotlin.String` as disclaimer content.

The extra typically contains one disclaimer from the company of mobile device management application (MDM), and one disclaimer from the organization.

Call `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Bundle.html#putParcelableArray(kotlin.String,%20kotlin.Array)` to put the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Bundle.html#`\[\]

Maximum 3 key-value pairs can be specified. The rest will be ignored.

Can be used in an intent with action `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.String`. This extra can also be returned by the admin app when performing the admin-integrated provisioning flow as a result of the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_GET_PROVISIONING_MODE:kotlin.String` activity.

 Value: "android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMERS"

### EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_CONTENT

Added in [API level 26](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_CONTENT: String
```

A `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/net/Uri.html#` extra pointing to disclaimer content.

##### The following URI schemes are accepted:

- content (`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/ContentResolver.html#SCHEME_CONTENT:kotlin.String`)
- android.resource (`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/ContentResolver.html#SCHEME_ANDROID_RESOURCE:kotlin.String`)

<br />

Styled text is supported. This is parsed by `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/text/Html.html#fromHtml(kotlin.String)` and displayed in a `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/widget/TextView.html#`.

If a `content:` URI is passed, the intent should also have the flag `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION:kotlin.Int` and the uri should be added to the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/ClipData.html#` of the intent.

`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/pm/ApplicationInfo.html#FLAG_SYSTEM:kotlin.Int` can also insert a disclaimer by declaring an application-level meta-data in `AndroidManifest.xml`.

For example:

```kotlin
<meta-data
       android:name="android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_CONTENT"
       android:resource="@string/disclaimer_content"
  />
```

This must be accompanied with another extra using the key `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_HEADER:kotlin.String`.

 Value: "android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_DISCLAIMER_CONTENT"

A `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/net/Uri.html#` extra pointing to a logo image. This image will be shown during the provisioning. If this extra is not passed, a default image will be shown.

**The following URI schemes are accepted:**

- content (`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/ContentResolver.html#SCHEME_CONTENT:kotlin.String`)
- android.resource (`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/ContentResolver.html#SCHEME_ANDROID_RESOURCE:kotlin.String`)

It is the responsibility of the caller to provide an image with a reasonable pixel density for the device.

If a content: URI is passed, the intent should also have the flag `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#FLAG_GRANT_READ_URI_PERMISSION:kotlin.Int` and the uri should be added to the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/ClipData.html#` of the intent.

 Value: "android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_LOGO_URI"

A boolean extra indicating the admin of a fully-managed device opts out of controlling permission grants for sensor-related permissions, see `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setPermissionGrantState(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.String,%20kotlin.String,%20kotlin.Int)`. ### EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SHOULD_LAUNCH_RESULT_INTENT

Added in [API level 33](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SHOULD_LAUNCH_RESULT_INTENT: String
```

A boolean extra that determines whether the provisioning flow should launch the resulting launch intent, if one is supplied by the device policy management role holder via `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_RESULT_LAUNCH_INTENT:kotlin.String`. Default value is `false`.

If `true`, the resulting intent will be launched by the provisioning flow, if one is supplied by the device policy management role holder.

If `false`, the resulting intent will be returned as `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_RESULT_LAUNCH_INTENT:kotlin.String` to the provisioning initiator, if one is supplied by the device manager role holder. It will be the responsibility of the provisioning initiator to launch this `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#` after provisioning completes.

This extra is respected when provided via the provisioning intent actions such as `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.String`.

 Value: "android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_SHOULD_LAUNCH_RESULT_INTENT"

```

A boolean extra indicating if the education screens from the provisioning flow should be skipped. If unspecified, defaults to `false`.

- For managed account enrollment

If the education screens are skipped, it is the admin application's responsibility to display its own user education screens.

### EXTRA_PROVISIONING_USE_MOBILE_DATA

Added in [API level 33](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val EXTRA_PROVISIONING_USE_MOBILE_DATA: String
```

A boolean extra indicating if mobile data should be used during the provisioning flow for downloading the admin app. If `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_SSID:kotlin.String` is also specified, wifi network will be used instead.

Default value is `false`.

If this extra is set to `true` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_SSID:kotlin.String` is not specified, this extra has different behaviour depending on the way provisioning is triggered:

- For provisioning started via a QR code or an NFC tag, mobile data is always used for downloading the admin app.
- For all other provisioning methods, a mobile data connection check is made at the start of provisioning. If mobile data is connected at that point, the admin app download will happen using mobile data. If mobile data is not connected at that point, the end-user will be asked to pick a wifi network and the admin app download will proceed over wifi.

 Value: "android.app.extra.PROVISIONING_USE_MOBILE_DATA"

static val EXTRA_RESULT_LAUNCH_INTENT: String
```

An `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#` result extra specifying the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#` to be launched after provisioning is finalized.

If `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_SHOULD_LAUNCH_RESULT_INTENT:kotlin.String` is set to `false`, this result will be supplied as part of the result `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#` for provisioning actions such as `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ACTION_PROVISION_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.String`. This result will also be supplied as part of the result `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/Intent.html#` for the device policy management role holder provisioning actions.

### FLAG_EVICT_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY

Added in [API level 26](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val FLAG_EVICT_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY: Int
```

Flag for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#lockNow(kotlin.Int)`: also evict the user's credential encryption key from the keyring. The user's credential will need to be entered again in order to derive the credential encryption key that will be stored back in the keyring for future use.

This flag can only be used by a profile owner when locking a managed profile when `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getStorageEncryptionStatus()` returns `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#ENCRYPTION_STATUS_ACTIVE_PER_USER:kotlin.Int`.

In order to secure user data, the user will be stopped and restarted so apps should wait until they are next run to perform further actions.

 Value: 1

### FLAG_MANAGED_CAN_ACCESS_PARENT

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val FLAG_MANAGED_CAN_ACCESS_PARENT: Int
```

Flag used by `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#addCrossProfileIntentFilter(android.content.ComponentName,%20android.content.IntentFilter,%20kotlin.Int)` to allow activities in the managed profile to access intents sent from the parent profile. That is, when an app in the parent profile calls android.app.Activity#startActivity(android.content.Intent), the intent can be resolved by a matching activity in the managed profile.

### MIME_TYPE_PROVISIONING_NFC

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val MIME_TYPE_PROVISIONING_NFC: String
```

This MIME type is used for starting the device owner provisioning.

During device owner provisioning a device admin app is set as the owner of the device. A device owner has full control over the device. The device owner can not be modified by the user and the only way of resetting the device is if the device owner app calls a factory reset.

A typical use case would be a device that is owned by a company, but used by either an employee or client.

The NFC message must be sent to an unprovisioned device.

The NFC record must contain a serialized `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/java/util/Properties.html#` object which contains the following properties:

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_NAME:kotlin.String`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_LOCATION:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_DOWNLOAD_COOKIE_HEADER:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_CHECKSUM:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LOCAL_TIME:kotlin.String` (convert to String), optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_TIME_ZONE:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_LOCALE:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_SSID:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_HIDDEN:kotlin.String` (convert to String), optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_SECURITY_TYPE:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_PASSWORD:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_PROXY_HOST:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_PROXY_PORT:kotlin.String` (convert to String), optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_PROXY_BYPASS:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_PAC_URL:kotlin.String`, optional
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_ADMIN_EXTRAS_BUNDLE:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#M:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_EAP_METHOD:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_PHASE2_AUTH:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_CA_CERTIFICATE:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_USER_CERTIFICATE:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_IDENTITY:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_ANONYMOUS_IDENTITY:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_WIFI_DOMAIN:kotlin.String`, optional, supported from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#Q:kotlin.Int`

As of `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#M:kotlin.Int`, the properties should contain `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_COMPONENT_NAME:kotlin.String` instead of `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_NAME:kotlin.String`, (although specifying only `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#EXTRA_PROVISIONING_DEVICE_ADMIN_PACKAGE_NAME:kotlin.String` is still supported).

 Value: "application/com.android.managedprovisioning"

### PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY_HIGH

Added in [API level 29](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
static val PASSWORD_COMPLEXITY_HIGH: Int
```

Constant for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getPasswordComplexity()` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setRequiredPasswordComplexity(kotlin.Int)`. Define the high password complexity band as:

- PIN with **no** repeating (4444) or ordered (1234, 4321, 2468) sequences, length at least 8
- alphabetic, length at least 6
- alphanumeric, length at least 6

<br />

When returned from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getPasswordComplexity()`, the constant represents the exact complexity band the password is in. When passed to `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setRequiredPasswordComplexity(kotlin.Int)`, it sets the minimum complexity band which the password must meet.

 Value: 327680

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#PASSWORD_QUALITY_NUMERIC_COMPLEX:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#PASSWORD_QUALITY_ALPHABETIC:kotlin.Int`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#PASSWORD_QUALITY_ALPHANUMERIC:kotlin.Int`

```

```

Flag for `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#resetPasswordWithToken(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.String,%20kotlin.ByteArray,%20kotlin.Int)` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#resetPassword(kotlin.String,%20kotlin.Int)`: don't ask for user credentials on device boot. If the flag is set, the device can be booted without asking for user password. The absence of this flag does not change the current boot requirements. This flag can be set by the device owner only. ## Public methods

### acknowledgeDeviceCompliant

Added in [API level 31](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
open fun acknowledgeDeviceCompliant(): Unit
```

Called by a profile owner of an organization-owned managed profile to acknowledge that the device is compliant and the user can turn the profile off if needed according to the maximum time off policy. This method should be called when the device is deemed compliant after getting `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver#onComplianceAcknowledgementRequired(android.content.Context,%20android.content.Intent)` callback in case it is overridden. Before this method is called the user is still free to turn the profile off, but the timer won't be reset, so personal apps will be suspended sooner. DPCs only need acknowledging device compliance if they override `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver#onComplianceAcknowledgementRequired(android.content.Context,%20android.content.Intent)`, otherwise compliance is acknowledged automatically.

| Exceptions ||
|---|---|
| `java.lang.IllegalStateException` | if the user isn't unlocked |

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#isComplianceAcknowledgementRequired()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setManagedProfileMaximumTimeOff(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Long)`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver#onComplianceAcknowledgementRequired(android.content.Context,%20android.content.Intent)`

### addCrossProfileIntentFilter

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
open fun addCrossProfileIntentFilter(
    admin: ComponentName?, 
    filter: IntentFilter!, 
    flags: Int
): Unit
```

Called by the profile owner of a managed profile so that some intents sent in the managed profile can also be resolved in the parent, or vice versa. Only activity intents are supported.

| Parameters ||
|---|---|
| `admin` | [ComponentName](../android/content/ComponentName.md)?: Which `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver` this request is associated with. This value may be `null`. |
| `filter` | [IntentFilter](../android/content/IntentFilter.md)!: The `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/IntentFilter.html#` the intent has to match to be also resolved in the other profile |
| `flags` | [Int](https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-int/index.html): `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#FLAG_MANAGED_CAN_ACCESS_PARENT:kotlin.Int` and `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#FLAG_PARENT_CAN_ACCESS_MANAGED:kotlin.Int` are supported. |
| --- | --- |

| Exceptions ||
|---|---|
| `java.lang.SecurityException` | if `admin` is not a device or profile owner. |

### addCrossProfileWidgetProvider

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
open fun addCrossProfileWidgetProvider(
    admin: ComponentName?, 
    packageName: String!
): Boolean
```

Called by the profile owner of a managed profile or a holder of the permission `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#MANAGE_DEVICE_POLICY_PROFILE_INTERACTION:kotlin.String` to enable widget providers from a given package to be available in the parent profile. As a result the user will be able to add widgets from the allowlisted package running under the profile to a widget host which runs under the parent profile, for example the home screen. Note that a package may have zero or more provider components, where each component provides a different widget type.

**Note:** By default no widget provider package is allowlisted. This API updates the allowlist incrementally. For better performance when updating multiple providers, use `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setCrossProfileWidgetProviders(kotlin.collections.MutableSet)`.

| Parameters ||
|---|---|
| `admin` | [ComponentName](../android/content/ComponentName.md)?: Which `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver` this request is associated with. Null if the caller is not a device admin. This value may be `null`. |
| `packageName` | [String](https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-string/index.html)!: The package from which widget providers are allowlisted. |

| Return ||
|---|---|
| `https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-boolean/index.html` | Whether the package was added. |

| Exceptions ||
|---|---|
| `java.lang.SecurityException` | if `admin` is not a profile owner and not a holder of the permission `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#MANAGE_DEVICE_POLICY_PROFILE_INTERACTION:kotlin.String`. |

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#removeCrossProfileWidgetProvider(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.String)`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getCrossProfileWidgetProviders(android.content.ComponentName)`

### addOverrideApn

Added in [API level 28](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
open fun addOverrideApn(
    admin: ComponentName, 
    apnSetting: ApnSetting
): Int
```

Called by device owner or managed profile owner to add an override APN.

This method may returns `-1` if `apnSetting` conflicts with an existing override APN. Update the existing conflicted APN with `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#updateOverrideApn(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Int,%20android.telephony.data.ApnSetting)` instead of adding a new entry.

Two override APNs are considered to conflict when all the following APIs return the same values on both override APNs:

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getOperatorNumeric()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getApnName()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getProxyAddressAsString()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getProxyPort()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getMmsProxyAddressAsString()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getMmsProxyPort()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getMmsc()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#isEnabled()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getMvnoType()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getProtocol()`
- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#getRoamingProtocol()`

Before Android version `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#TIRAMISU:kotlin.Int`: Only device owners can add APNs.

Starting from Android version `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#TIRAMISU:kotlin.Int`: Both device owners and managed profile owners can add enterprise APNs (`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.html#TYPE_ENTERPRISE:kotlin.Int`), while only device owners can add other type of APNs. Enterprise APNs are specific to the managed profile and do not override any user-configured VPNs. They are prerequisites for enabling preferential network service on the managed profile on 4G networks (`https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setPreferentialNetworkServiceConfigs(kotlin.collections.MutableList)`).

| Parameters ||
|---|---|
| `admin` | [ComponentName](../android/content/ComponentName.md): which `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver` this request is associated with. This value cannot be `null`. |
| `apnSetting` | [ApnSetting](../android/telephony/data/ApnSetting.md): the override APN to insert. This value cannot be `null`. |

| Return ||
|---|---|
| `https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-int/index.html` | The `id` of inserted override APN. Or `-1` when failed to insert into the database. |

| Exceptions ||
|---|---|
| `java.lang.SecurityException` | If request is for enterprise APN `admin` is either device owner or profile owner and in all other types of APN if `admin` is not a device owner. |

**See Also**

- `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#setOverrideApnsEnabled(android.content.ComponentName,%20kotlin.Boolean)`

### addPersistentPreferredActivity

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
open fun addPersistentPreferredActivity(
    admin: ComponentName?, 
    filter: IntentFilter!, 
    activity: ComponentName
): Unit
```

Called by a profile owner or device owner or holder of the permission `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#MANAGE_DEVICE_POLICY_LOCK_TASK:kotlin.String`. to set a default activity that the system selects to handle intents that match the given `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/content/IntentFilter.html#` instead of showing the default disambiguation mechanism. This activity will remain the default intent handler even if the set of potential event handlers for the intent filter changes and if the intent preferences are reset.

Note that the target application should still declare the activity in the manifest, the API just sets the activity to be the default one to handle the given intent filter.

The default disambiguation mechanism takes over if the activity is not installed (anymore). When the activity is (re)installed, it is automatically reset as default intent handler for the filter.

Note that calling this API to set a default intent handler, only allow to avoid the default disambiguation mechanism. Implicit intents that do not trigger this mechanism (like invoking the browser) cannot be configured as they are controlled by other configurations.

The calling device admin must be a profile owner or device owner. If it is not, a security exception will be thrown.

Starting from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE:kotlin.Int`, after the persistent preferred activity policy has been set, `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateReceiver#onPolicySetResult(android.content.Context,%20kotlin.String,%20android.os.Bundle,%20android.app.admin.TargetUser,%20android.app.admin.PolicyUpdateResult)` will notify the admin on whether the policy was successfully set or not. This callback will contain:

- The policy identifier `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyIdentifiers#PERSISTENT_PREFERRED_ACTIVITY_POLICY:kotlin.String`
- The additional policy params bundle, which contains `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateReceiver#EXTRA_INTENT_FILTER:kotlin.String` the intent filter the policy applies to
- The `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/TargetUser` that this policy relates to
- The `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult`, which will be `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult#RESULT_POLICY_SET:kotlin.Int` if the policy was successfully set or the reason the policy failed to be set (e.g. `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult#RESULT_FAILURE_CONFLICTING_ADMIN_POLICY:kotlin.Int`)

If there has been a change to the policy, `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateReceiver#onPolicyChanged(android.content.Context,%20kotlin.String,%20android.os.Bundle,%20android.app.admin.TargetUser,%20android.app.admin.PolicyUpdateResult)` will notify the admin of this change. This callback will contain the same parameters as PolicyUpdateReceiver#onPolicySetResult and the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult` will contain the reason why the policy changed.

NOTE: Performs disk I/O and shouldn't be called on the main thread.

| Parameters ||
|---|---|
| `admin` | [ComponentName](../android/content/ComponentName.md)?: Which `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver` this request is associated with. Null if the caller is not a device admin. This value may be `null`. |
| `filter` | [IntentFilter](../android/content/IntentFilter.md)!: The IntentFilter for which a default handler is added. |
| `activity` | [ComponentName](../android/content/ComponentName.md): The Activity that is added as default intent handler. This value cannot be `null`. |
| --- | --- |

| Exceptions ||
|---|---|
| `java.lang.SecurityException` | if `admin` is not a device or profile owner or holder of the permission `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/Manifest.permission.html#MANAGE_DEVICE_POLICY_LOCK_TASK:kotlin.String`. |

### addUserRestriction

Added in [API level 21](https://developer.android.com/guide/topics/manifest/uses-sdk-element.html#ApiLevels)

```
open fun addUserRestriction(
    admin: ComponentName?, 
    key: String!
): Unit
```

Called by a profile owner, device owner or a holder of any permission that is associated with a user restriction to set a user restriction specified by the key.

The calling device admin must be a profile owner, device owner or holder of any permission that is associated with a user restriction; if it is not, a security exception will be thrown.

The profile owner of an organization-owned managed profile may invoke this method on the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#` instance it obtained from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyManager#getParentProfileInstance(android.content.ComponentName)`, for enforcing device-wide restrictions.

See the constants in `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#` for the list of restrictions that can be enforced device-wide. These constants will also state in their documentation which permission is required to manage the restriction using this API.

Starting from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/Build.VERSION_CODES.html#UPSIDE_DOWN_CAKE:kotlin.Int`, after the user restriction policy has been set, `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateReceiver#onPolicySetResult(android.content.Context,%20kotlin.String,%20android.os.Bundle,%20android.app.admin.TargetUser,%20android.app.admin.PolicyUpdateResult)` will notify the admin on whether the policy was successfully set or not. This callback will contain:

- The policy identifier returned from `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DevicePolicyIdentifiers#getIdentifierForUserRestriction(kotlin.String)`
- The `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/TargetUser` that this policy relates to
- The `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult`, which will be `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult#RESULT_POLICY_SET:kotlin.Int` if the policy was successfully set or the reason the policy failed to be set (e.g. `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult#RESULT_FAILURE_CONFLICTING_ADMIN_POLICY:kotlin.Int`)

If there has been a change to the policy, `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateReceiver#onPolicyChanged(android.content.Context,%20kotlin.String,%20android.os.Bundle,%20android.app.admin.TargetUser,%20android.app.admin.PolicyUpdateResult)` will notify the admin of this change. This callback will contain the same parameters as PolicyUpdateReceiver#onPolicySetResult and the `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/PolicyUpdateResult` will contain the reason why the policy changed.

| Parameters ||
|---|---|
| `admin` | [ComponentName](../android/content/ComponentName.md)?: Which `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/app/admin/DeviceAdminReceiver` this request is associated with or `null` if the caller is not a device admin. |
| `key` | [String](https://kotlinlang.org/api/latest/jvm/stdlib/kotlin/-string/index.html)!: The key of the restriction. Value is one of the following: - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#ALLOW_PARENT_PROFILE_APP_LINKING:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_ADD_MANAGED_PROFILE:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_ADD_PRIVATE_PROFILE:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_ADD_USER:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_ADD_WIFI_CONFIG:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_ADJUST_VOLUME:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_AIRPLANE_MODE:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_AMBIENT_DISPLAY:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_APPS_CONTROL:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_ASSIST_CONTENT:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_AUTOFILL:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_BLUETOOTH:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_BLUETOOTH_SHARING:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_CAMERA_TOGGLE:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_CHANGE_WIFI_STATE:kotlin.String` - `https://developer.android.com/reference/kotlin/android/os/UserManager.html#DISALLOW_CONFIG_BLUETOOTH:kotlin.String` -
